whale-watching.how: Whale watching in Tokyo Metropolis means the Ogasawara Islands, about 1,000 km away on a roughly 24-hour ferry; there is no regular whale-watching in Tokyo Bay.

piano.how: Shimamura Music Store's Ikebukuro Piano Salon gives private adult piano lessons in English, with a 30-minute trial.

amateur-radio.how: The Japan Amateur Radio League (JARL), the national ham body, is headquartered in Tokyo and supports licensing and local clubs.

ctf-security.how: SECCON runs Japan's national CTF series, with an on-site final held in the Tokyo area in past years.

coding-meetups.how: connpass lists a steady stream of developer study groups and meetups held across Tokyo.

hackathons.how: Hackathons and game-jam style events are regularly listed on connpass for Tokyo venues.

laser-cutting.how: FabCafe Tokyo is a Shibuya cafe where visitors book laser cutters and UV printers for digital fabrication.

arcade-games.how: Taito Station runs game centres across Tokyo, including the Akihabara arcade district.

board-games.how: Jelly Jelly Cafe runs board game cafes with a large library at over a dozen Tokyo branches, including Shibuya, Shinjuku and Akihabara.

contract-bridge.how: The Japan Contract Bridge League is the national federation and lists clubs and tournaments.

cosplay.how: Comiket, the huge doujin convention at Tokyo Big Sight, has a large cosplay area, and cosplay events recur around Akihabara and Ikebukuro.

escape-rooms.how: SCRAP's Real Escape Game pioneered puzzle-escape events and runs them at Tokyo venues.

go-weiqi.how: The Nihon Ki-in, Japan's Go association, is based in Tokyo and runs a Go salon and classes.

trading-card-games.how: Hareruya is a major Magic: The Gathering retailer in Tokyo with in-store play spaces and tournaments.

speedcubing.how: WCA-sanctioned speedcubing competitions are held in Tokyo several times a year.

ten-pin-bowling.how: Round1 runs large bowling alleys across the Tokyo area with shoe rental.

vr-gaming.how: Tokyo Joypolis, a Sega indoor amusement park in Odaiba, includes VR attractions.

beekeeping-honey.how: The Ginza Honeybee Project keeps rooftop hives in central Tokyo and harvests Ginza honey.

pasta-and-general-cooking-classes.how: ABC Cooking Studio runs hands-on cooking classes at studios across Tokyo.

tea-ceremony.how: Happo-en's garden tea room Yume-an serves tea in a traditional setting, and tea ceremony experiences are widely offered in Tokyo.

archival-research.how: The National Archives of Japan holds government records in Kitanomaru Park and has a reading room open to the public.

art-gallery.how: The Mori Art Museum atop Roppongi Hills shows contemporary art exhibitions.

history-walks.how: Tokyo Free Guide connects visitors with volunteer local guides for walking tours.

japanese-language.how: Genki Japanese and Culture School runs Japanese courses for foreigners at its Tokyo campus.

spanish-language.how: Instituto Cervantes Tokyo offers Spanish courses.

museums.how: The Tokyo National Museum in Ueno is Japan's oldest and largest museum.

moocs.how: JMOOC offers Japanese-language online courses free of location constraints; this is not a Tokyo-specific venue.

science-museum.how: Miraikan, the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation, is in Odaiba.

wartime-history.how: The Center of the Tokyo Air Raids and War Damage documents the 1945 firebombing of Tokyo.
wartime-history.venue: Center of the Tokyo Raids and War Damage

dog-parks.how: Yoyogi Park has a dedicated dog run among its facilities.

parkour.how: The Japan Parkour Association publishes guidance on practising in public spaces and supports the Tokyo community.

hot-spring-bathing.how: Spa LaQua at Tokyo Dome City advertises a natural hot spring bath.

onsen.how: Tokyo has many sento public bathhouses, plus onsen-style spas such as Spa LaQua.

sauna.how: Spa LaQua at Tokyo Dome City includes a sauna lounge among its facilities.

temple-activities.how: Senso-ji in Asakusa is Tokyo's oldest temple and open to worshippers and visitors.

volunteering.how: The Tokyo Volunteer and Civic Activity Center matches residents with volunteer opportunities.
volunteering.venue: Tokyo Volunteer and Civic Activity Center

drone-racing.how: Drone racing events have been held in Tokyo (an FAI-sanctioned race at Tokyo Big Sight in 2019) and DJI opened an indoor flying arena in 2017; regular leagues mainly race in neighbouring Chiba.

outdoor-rock-climbing.how: Mount Mitake in Ome, western Tokyo prefecture, is a bouldering area described as the nearest to the city; sport and trad areas such as Ogawayama and Mizugaki are 3+ hours away.

hydroponics-urban-farming.how: Urban farm experiences and rental community garden plots operate in Tokyo, e.g. the Yakumo no Hatake community garden in Meguro and rooftop and hydroponic workshops.

mushroom-foraging.how: Pick-your-own mushroom gardens exist in the Tama area (Uchinuma Kinoko-en), but guided wild mushroom foraging was not found.

dragon-boat.how: Tokyo Dragon Boat Tournament is held at Odaiba Kaihin Park with full support for first-time teams; the Sea Forest Waterway is also used for dragon boating.
dragon-boat.venue: Tokyo Dragon Boat Tournament (Odaiba Kaihin Park)

wakeboarding.how: Cable wakeboarding has been staged in Tokyo (a Cable Wakeboard World Cup at Odaiba under Rainbow Bridge); regular wakeboarding parks are mostly in surrounding prefectures.

drone-flying.how: Recreational drone flying is legal in Japan under MLIT rules (registration for drones over 100 g, restrictions in dense areas), with riverside and park spots used around Tokyo.

acting.how: English-language acting workshops (a one-day intensive by UPS) and weekly improv classes at Tokyo Comedy School near Yoyogi-Koen are available.

tango.how: Argentine tango lessons run at studios such as Doble A in Sengoku, taught by former Buenos Aires Tango Pista champions.

bharatanatyam.how: The Vivekananda Cultural Centre at the Embassy of India in Tokyo has held workshops and lessons in Indian classical dance including Bharatanatyam.
bharatanatyam.venue: Vivekananda Cultural Centre, Embassy of India

tabla.how: The Vivekananda Cultural Centre at the Embassy of India in Tokyo has run tabla workshops and lessons.
tabla.venue: Vivekananda Cultural Centre, Embassy of India

pole-dance.how: Art Flow Tokyo is a pole and aerial dance studio with classes from beginner to advanced, and Rei Dance Collection also runs pole classes in Shibuya.

dj-turntablism.how: Tokyo VIBESRECORDS in Setagaya offers DJ lessons with a professional instructor, including a short beginner session with hands-on practice.

choir.how: Choirs such as Tokyo Musik Kreis and the Bach Akademie Meiji Gakuin Tokyo chorus draw singers from across the city.

gamelan.how: Over 50 Indonesian gamelan groups exist in Japan, with Indonesian performing arts shown in Tokyo most weekends.

guitar.how: Guitar lessons in English and Japanese are offered in Tokyo, e.g. American Guitar Academy (Roppongi, Sendagi) and JiLL Music School (Shibuya, Ikebukuro).

ikebana.how: The Sogetsu Foundation at its Tokyo headquarters offers hands-on ikebana lessons with a master instructor in English or Japanese, and many English-speaking instructors teach private classes.

kintsugi.how: Short hands-on kintsugi workshops with English-speaking instructors run in Asakusa (Kuge Crafts Studio) and other Tokyo studios.

lampworking.how: Tokyo booking platforms list glass-bead making experiences alongside Edo kiriko glass cutting.

perfumery.how: Custom perfume blending sessions run in Monzen-Nakacho, Asakusa, Omotesando and Harajuku, with a certified blend designer in some.

snow-sculpture.how: Tokyo gets almost no lasting snow, so snow sculpting is not possible locally; the nearest large-scale venue is the Sapporo Snow Festival in Hokkaido, about 1.5 hours by air.

3d-printing.how: FabCafe Tokyo in Shibuya offers digital fabrication including 3D printing and laser cutting to visitors.

cnc-machining.how: FabCafe Tokyo's MTRL workspace in Shibuya offers prototyping and digital fabrication machines and materials.

game-development-jams.how: Game jams and developer study events are regularly listed on connpass for Tokyo venues.

fireworks-pyrotechnics.how: Hobby fireworks making is not available: manufacturing explosives requires licences under Japan's explosives control law, so fireworks are made only by licensed professional makers.

model-rocketry.how: University clubs such as Tokyo Tech's CREATE rocketry club build and launch rockets near Tokyo, and occasional public model rocket workshops run in the Kanagawa area.

robotics-arduino.how: Maker Faire Tokyo and maker spaces such as FabCafe support electronics, Arduino and Raspberry Pi projects, and Akihabara is Japan's electronics parts district.
robotics-arduino.venue: Maker Faire Tokyo / Akihabara electronics shops

dungeons-and-dragons.how: Tokyo Tabletop, a Meetup-based group, hosts weekly tabletop gaming sessions in Shibuya including roleplaying games.

mahjong.how: Mahjong parlours (jansou) are common across Tokyo, and the Japan Professional Mahjong Association is based in the city.

pub-trivia.how: TELL Pub Quiz runs a regular English-language quiz night in Tokyo, held at the Footnik pub in Osaki.

chocolate-making.how: Green Bean to Bar Chocolate in Nakameguro makes chocolate from the bean and has run workshops on the production process.

artisan-bread-baking.how: Home bakeries in Tokyo run bread and shokupan baking classes for visitors via booking platforms such as ByFood and Rakuten Experiences.

sourdough-baking.how: Natural-yeast bread classes are offered by home bakeries in Setagaya through Rakuten Experiences.

homebrewing-beer.how: Hitachino Brewing Lab near Akihabara offers hands-on beer classes alongside its taproom, while home brewing is limited by Japanese alcohol-tax rules.

mixology.how: The Nippon Bartenders Association is based in Tokyo and the city has a dense cocktail bar scene, including Ginza bars.

coffee-roasting.how: Home coffee-roasting experiences are offered by former baristas in Ota City, Tokyo, via Airbnb Experiences.

sake-making.how: Toshimaya Brewery in Musashimurayama, western Tokyo, offers guided tours of its sake production with tastings, but hands-on brewing is not confirmed for the public.

sake-tasting.how: Toshimaya Brewery, founded 1596 in western Tokyo, runs guided tours ending with sake tastings, and Tokyo has many sake bars.

sushi-making.how: Tokyo has many beginner sushi-making classes, including sessions tied to Tsukiji fish market where participants make nigiri and maki with a professional chef.

fermentation-kombucha.how: Fermentation is central to Japanese food and sake brewery tours exist, but a regular kombucha or kimchi class is not confirmed.

vinyl-records.how: Tokyo is a major vinyl market with large record-store districts such as Shibuya and Shinjuku, home to chains like Disk Union.

book-club.how: Tokyo English Book Exchange and similar groups meet in Shibuya to swap and discuss English books.

creative-writing.how: Tokyo Writers Workshop meets monthly in English to critique fiction and poetry, and Tokyo Poetry Journal lists creative writing workshops.

poetry-slam.how: Tokyo Poetry Journal (ToPoJo) lists poetry readings and events at Tokyo venues.

language-exchange.how: Language exchange and English book-swap meetups run regularly in Tokyo.

toastmasters.how: Toastmasters International lists English and Japanese clubs across Tokyo.

public-lectures.how: The University of Tokyo and other Tokyo universities hold public lectures and symposia for general audiences.

meetups.how: Tokyo has large Meetup-based communities, such as Tokyo Tabletop with over 4,000 members, plus connpass events.

running-club.how: HOUYHNHNM Running Club runs a running station in Nihonbashi Hamacho with Sumida River routes.

cold-plunge.how: Toshimaen Niwa-no-yu in Meguro and other Tokyo saunas and sento provide cold plunge pools.

fencing.how: Listed in OpenStreetMap: TOKYO FENCING (nearest of 1 tagged venues within 20 km); not checked for current opening.

bmx.how: Ariake Urban Sports Park, built for the Tokyo 2020 BMX racing and freestyle events, has reopened as a public leisure and sports park with skate and sports facilities; BMX-specific public sessions were not confirmed.

padel.how: PADEL TOKYO mizumachi, opened by Tobu Railway in 2023 under the Skytree line in east Tokyo, offers padel courts for hire.

rock-climbing-top-rope.how: B-PUMP Tokyo Akihabara is one of Japan's largest climbing gyms with daily first-timer lessons; Tokyo also has many rope-climbing gyms, though top-rope at B-PUMP specifically was not confirmed.

glassblowing.how: Tokyo Glass Art in Ota Ward runs short walk-in glassblowing experiences where visitors blow their own piece.

oil-painting.how: Artbar Tokyo in Daikanyama runs painting sessions in English and Japanese, and International Art Studio in Minato offers painting and drawing classes in English.

watercolour-painting.how: Artbar Tokyo runs casual painting-and-drink sessions (watercolour sessions not specifically confirmed); Japanese-language art schools offer dedicated watercolour courses.

sailing.how: Wakasu Yacht Training School operates from a boathouse inside Wakasu Seaside Park on Tokyo Bay, run under the Tokyo metropolitan government; Sailability Tokyo also runs Hansa dinghy sessions at Toyosu.

dinghy-sailing.how: Wakasu Yacht Training School in Wakasu Seaside Park teaches dinghy sailing on Tokyo Bay, and Hansa 303 dinghy sessions run from Toyosu.

camping.how: Wakasu Seaside Park has a metropolitan-run camping ground on Tokyo Bay, and larger campsites operate in the Tama and Okutama areas.

gaelic-football-hurling.how: Japan GAA, a volunteer-run club founded in 1995 with 300+ members, plays Gaelic football (and hurling) in Tokyo and welcomes new players.

etching.how: Printmaking workshop Fuji Graphics in Taito offers one-off experiences choosing lithography, silkscreen or copperplate etching, and Machida City Museum of Graphic Arts runs a one-day etching (drypoint) course for beginners.

lithography.how: Printmaking workshop Fuji Graphics in Taito offers lithography experiences, and the Machida City Museum of Graphic Arts print studio runs lithography courses.

printmaking-screenprint.how: Printmaking workshop Fuji Graphics in Taito offers a 2-4 hour silkscreen experience for up to six people by reservation.

stained-glass.how: Beginner stained glass experiences run at several studios, such as Stainedglass Pastel in Taito, Atelier T&T in Setagaya and Stained House Amaud in Kunitachi.

irish-dance.how: Ardagh School of Irish Dance teaches in Tokyo, the first CLRG-accredited Irish dance school in Japan, taking children and adults from beginner to competitive level.

pet-adoption.how: Rescue groups such as Buddies, ARK and Japan Cat Network place dogs and cats with adopters in Tokyo, with English-language processes for international residents.

animal-shelter-volunteering.how: Tokyo rescue groups such as ARK and Buddies accept volunteers and foster families, but a dedicated English-language shelter volunteer programme was not confirmed.

meditation.how: Zen temples and groups run English beginner zazen in and around Tokyo, including Dogen Sangha (Saturday sessions), Tokozenji and Sojiji in Yokohama, and Denchuji.

hackerspace-electronics.how: Shibuya has a cluster of public making spaces including FabLab Shibuya and FabCafe (part of Tokyo Fabbers) with 3D printers, laser cutters and electronics tools, and Tokyo Hackerspace-style groups meet regularly.

candle-making.how: Candle Studio RADIUS in Chiyoda's Sanbancho runs candle-making classes, including Japanese-sweets aroma candles, by reservation.

whisky-tasting.how: TOKYO Whisky Library in Omotesando is a whisky lounge with over 1,000 bottles and a menu of tasting flights and staff who explain the selection.

wine-tasting-wset.how: Fine Vintage runs WSET Level 1 and 2 wine courses in Tokyo at the Westin Tokyo, and Academie du Vin Aoyama in Shibuya hosts WSET sake awards.
wine-tasting-wset.venue: Fine Vintage WSET at Westin Tokyo

chess.how: The Japan Chess Federation (formerly National Chess Society of Japan) has a Chess Center in Ueno, Taito, and runs events such as the Tokyo Chess Festival; informal meetups also run at pubs.

esports-gaming.how: Akihabara has e-sports Square and exeField Akiba gaming venues with banks of gaming PCs for play and tournaments, and Konami runs an esports arena in Ginza.

watchmaking-horology.how: Hiko Mizuno College of Jewelry near Shibuya Station runs 2- and 3-year WOSTEP-affiliated watchmaking courses.

kite-flying.how: The Kite Museum Tokyo (Taimeiken) in Nihonbashi holds 100+ kites with kite-making demonstrations and classes, and Wakasu Seaside Park and riverbank parks have open areas for flying.

orienteering.how: The Tokyo Orienteering Association and the Tama Orienteering Club organise park and urban orienteering events in the Tokyo area, such as the All Japan Trail Orienteering Championships at Nogawa Park, plus student-run Tokyo Orienteering events.

indoor-snow-play.how: No indoor snow slope operates in central Tokyo (the Funabashi ski dome closed), but Sayama Ski Resort in Saitama has a 300 m indoor slope about 40-60 minutes by train and Snova Shin-Yokohama has a 60 m slope.

stamp-collecting.how: The Philatelic Museum (Kitte no Hakubutsukan) in Mejiro holds around 350,000 stamps, with a specialist library and changing exhibitions.

cricket.how: The Japan Cricket Association is headquartered in Minato and runs leagues with Tokyo clubs (Tokyo Wombats, Tokyo Titans, university teams), with Akishima a designated cricket city, but the main international ground at Sano is 80-90 km away.

breakdancing.how: Shibuya street dance studios such as En Dance Studio hold regular classes, and Tokyo's breaking scene is described as one of the world's biggest, with Shibuya battles.

rock-fossil-collecting.how: The National Museum of Nature and Science in Ueno has Earth-history galleries and hands-on programmes for viewing fossils and specimens; field collecting sites are outside Tokyo.
rock-fossil-collecting.venue: National Museum of Nature and Science

capoeira.how: Capoeira Club London (founded 2012 by Mestre Hiram Ribeiro) runs around 40 classes a week across the city, alongside Cordao de Ouro and Grupo Muzenza.

silat.how: Traditional Bela Deri silat meets weekly at SOAS and sport-focused pencak silat runs in Walthamstow, open to beginners.

treetop-walk.how: Kew Gardens has a Treetop Walkway about 200 m long, roughly 18 m above ground in a woodland canopy.

dragon-boat.how: Raging Dragons trains on Sunday mornings at the Docklands Sailing and Watersports Centre and invites newcomers to try dragon boating.

wakeboarding.how: Wakeup Docklands runs a 2-point cable wakeboarding system in the Royal Docks with beginner (Blue) 15-minute sessions.

cable-skiing.how: Cable towing in London is wakeboard-oriented at Wakeup Docklands; no dedicated cable water-ski operation was confirmed.

stand-up-paddleboarding.how: Wakeup Docklands offers a one-hour Introduction to Paddleboarding for complete beginners plus a BSUPA Ready2Ride course and private SUP hire.

chinese-orchestra.how: The Long Walk Chinese Orchestra accepts beginners and experienced players, with music leaders teaching ruan, liuqin, erhu, pipa and dizi.

erhu.how: The UK Chinese Music Ensemble and London Youlan Qin Society offer erhu classes at beginner and intermediate levels, plus a summer school at SOAS.

guzheng.how: The UK Chinese Music Ensemble and London Youlan Qin Society offer guzheng classes at beginner and intermediate levels, plus a summer school at SOAS.

aerial-silks-circus.how: London Dance Academy runs beginner aerial silks courses in five-week blocks, and Aerial Gymnastics London teaches adult silks and hoop in Beckton.

pole-dance.how: Studios such as Akila Pole Studio and The Factory London and university clubs run beginner pole classes.

sup-yoga.how: Wakeup Docklands offers paddleboarding in the Royal Docks and its site shows yoga on a deck, but SUP yoga is not listed as a bookable session.

bobsled.how: Needs an ice track; none in the UK. Nearest are in Germany, Austria and Switzerland (about 2 hours by air).

buzkashi.how: Central Asian horseback game rooted in Afghanistan and neighbouring regions; no organised play near London.

camel-racing.how: Needs camel racing culture and tracks; nearest are in the Gulf, about 6 to 7 hours by air.

elephant-polo.how: Needs working elephants; played in Nepal, Thailand and India, 8+ hours by air.

ski-jumping.how: Needs a large hill and snow-covered jump; none in the UK. Nearest are in Germany and Norway, about 2 hours by air.

big-wall-climbing.how: No big walls in southern England; nearest are in the Alps or Norway, about 2 hours by air.

cheese-rolling.how: Cooper's Hill Cheese-Rolling happens once a year in Gloucestershire, about 160 km west of London (around 2.5 hours by car).

outdoor-rock-climbing.how: No natural crags within 30 km; the nearest sandstone outcrops (Harrison's Rocks, Sussex) are about 60 km away (around 1.5 hours by car).

mangrove-sea-kayaking.how: Mangroves need a tropical or subtropical coast; none in the UK.

salsa-bachata.how: Weekly beginner salsa and bachata classes followed by social dancing, no partner or booking needed.
salsa-bachata.venue: Earl's Court Salsa & Bachata Club (Incognito Dance Company)

sitar.how: The Bhavan Centre teaches Indian classical instruments including sitar as part of its music courses.

tabla.how: The Bhavan Centre lists tabla tuition and hosts tabla teacher recitals; independent teachers also offer private lessons.

stand-up-comedy.how: The Comedy Store runs a six-week beginners' stand-up course ending in a showcase set, plus a monthly open mic.

swing-lindy-hop.how: Weekly Lindy hop beginner classes with social dancing at club nights such as Swingland's A-Train.
swing-lindy-hop.venue: Swingland A-Train at The Hammersmith Club

taiko.how: Taiko Meantime, founded in Greenwich, teaches Japanese drumming with London sessions on request while regular classes are in Surrey.

tap-dance.how: Drop-in and short-course adult tap classes run at Pineapple Dance Studios, including a six-week beginner course.

chinese-opera.how: Community groups stage Cantonese opera in London (Croydon Chinese Community's Lotus Stars, Islington Chinese Association), but regular classes are not documented.

filmmaking.how: Raindance runs filmmaking courses in directing, producing and screenwriting from its London base.

glassblowing.how: London Glassblowing offers a glassblowing experience class at its Bermondsey studio and gallery.

robotics-arduino.how: London Hackspace hosts events on topics from electronics to biohacking for members and guests.

dim-sum-making.how: Beginner and advanced dim sum cooking classes run at London cookery venues, listed on ClassBento.

fermentation-kombucha.how: Monthly low-cost kimchi fermentation workshops run in South London where participants make a jar to take home; kombucha classes not confirmed.

tea-ceremony.how: A tea-master-led Japanese tea ceremony session runs in East London as an Airbnb Experience; the Japan Society also lists practitioners.

sake-tasting.how: Guided sake tastings with food pairing or cocktails run at London restaurants and bars.
sake-tasting.venue: La Bibliotheque sake and food pairing (ClassBento)

sourdough-baking.how: Half-day sourdough bread workshops run in London and are listed on Experience Days and ClassBento.

sushi-making.how: Beginner sushi-making workshops run in London (Archway, Trafalgar Square) and are listed on ClassBento.

comic-collecting.how: Specialist comic shops such as Forbidden Planet in central London sell back issues and collectibles.

rock-fossil-collecting.how: The Natural History Museum holds major fossil and mineral collections and is free to enter.

vinyl-records.how: London has dozens of independent record shops including Rough Trade East, Phonica and Reckless Records.

whale-watching.how: Dolphins, porpoises and seals are occasionally seen in the tidal Thames and ZSL runs a public marine mammal survey, but no organised whale-watching trips exist.

archival-research.how: The public can consult archives at the London Metropolitan Archives.

cultural-heritage-centres.how: Japan House London presents Japanese culture through exhibitions, talks and workshops.

genealogy.how: Family history research is supported by the Society of Genealogists and the London Metropolitan Archives.

public-lectures.how: Gresham College gives free public lectures in the City of London.

toastmasters.how: Toastmasters International operates multiple clubs across London.

wartime-history.how: Churchill War Rooms run by the Imperial War Museums show WWII command bunkers.

coastal-cleanup.how: Thames21 mobilises volunteers along the tidal Thames and other rivers for litter and monitoring events.

cold-plunge.how: Open-water cold swimming is available at the Hampstead Heath ponds, which are open year round.

meditation.how: Meditation classes run at the London Buddhist Centre.

pet-adoption.how: Battersea rehomes dogs and cats from its London centre.

running-club.how: parkrun free weekly 5k events and local clubs operate across London.

temple-activities.how: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Neasden holds services and is open to visitors.

urban-exploration.how: Guided Hidden London tours of disused Underground stations are run by the London Transport Museum; independent urban exploration is informal.

volunteering.how: Thames21 and other charities recruit volunteers across London.

base-jumping.how: No legal jump sites near London; BASE jumping means travelling to the Alps or similar.

bullfighting.how: Bullfighting is not practised in the UK; nearest tradition is in Spain or France.

cable-wakeboarding.how: Cable wakeboarding at WakeUp Docklands with beginner sessions.

canyoning.how: No canyons near London; nearest options are in Wales, about 4 hours away.

cave-diving.how: No flooded caves near London; nearest are the Mendips, about 3 hours away.

cave-exploring.how: No natural caves in the London basin; nearest caving is the Mendips, about 3 hours away.

dog-sledding.how: Needs snow and sled dog culture; none near London.

glacier-trekking.how: No glaciers in the UK; nearest are in the Alps or Iceland.

indoor-snow-play.how: Real-snow indoor slopes exist outside the metro area, such as Hemel Hempstead, roughly 40 km away.

luge.how: No luge track in the UK; nearest are abroad.

mountaineering.how: Mountaineering means travelling to Snowdonia, the Lake District or the Alps; only indoor walls exist in London.

outdoor-skydiving.how: Nearest drop zones such as Headcorn in Kent are around 70 km away, outside the metro area.

rodeo.how: Rodeo is not part of UK culture and no venues operate near London.

sandboarding-desert.how: No dunes or desert near London.

white-water-rafting.how: Lee Valley White Water Centre in Waltham Cross offers rafting on the Olympic course.

snowboarding.how: Group snowboard lessons and sessions run on the dry slope at The Oakwood (formerly Sandown Ski) in Esher; The Snow Centre in Hemel Hempstead offers real-snow lessons about 40 km out.

snow-skiing.how: Ski school with group lessons, private coaching and recreational sessions on a dry slope at The Oakwood in Esher; real-snow indoor slope at The Snow Centre, Hemel Hempstead (about 40 km).

drone-racing.how: Imperial College Drone Society runs an FPV racing team in London; the Grey Arrows Drone Club is a London flying association for racing quads and FPV, and London has hosted pro races at Wembley and Alexandra Palace.

drone-flying.how: Recreational drone flying is organised through London flying clubs such as the Grey Arrows Drone Club (public liability insurance for members) and the Imperial College Drone Society; UK flyer registration rules apply.

guitar.how: Guitar lessons for all ages and levels (acoustic, electric, classical, bass) are taught at London Guitar Academy in Hampstead and at London School of Music.

piano.how: Piano lessons are offered by London School of Music alongside guitar, singing and drums, in person or online.

harp.how: Guildhall School of Music & Drama has a dedicated harp department (conservatoire level); casual teachers are listed privately.

freshwater-fishing.how: Walthamstow Wetlands (Thames Water fishery) sells day tickets for coarse and trout fishing on its reservoirs; an Environment Agency rod licence is needed.

fishing-pond.how: The Angling Academy tuition pond at Walthamstow Wetlands runs family-friendly paid fishing sessions; the wider fishery sells day tickets for stocked rainbow trout.

scuba-diving.how: Oyster Diving in Soho runs PADI Discover Scuba and Open Water courses with pool sessions at Marshall Street Leisure Centre; open-water dives are done at inland sites outside London.

camping.how: Lee Valley Camping and Caravan Park in Edmonton is a tent and caravan site inside the London boundary; Abbey Wood and Crystal Palace also have camping and caravan sites.

nature-guided-walks.how: Friends of Richmond Park run a free two-hour guided walk, and The Royal Parks and the Mayor of London publish self-guided nature trails.
nature-guided-walks.venue: Friends of Richmond Park guided walk

trail-running.how: Hampstead Heath, Richmond Park and Bushy Park have off-road running routes listed by Great Runs, with parkrun events weekly.

flamenco.how: City Lit runs flamenco courses in its Covent Garden dance studios in daytime, evening and weekend slots; Ritmo Flamenco teaches in Greenwich.

tango.how: Corrientes Social Club in Greenwich teaches Argentine tango classes, and Tango South London runs Monday and Tuesday night classes.

etching.how: City Lit's Keeley Street printmaking studio has two intaglio roll presses and runs beginner to advanced etching, drypoint and aquatint courses.

lithography.how: City Lit runs stone and photo lithography workshops, including a three-day photo lithography course, in its Keeley Street studio.

bagpipes.how: Private bagpipe tutors in London (including Earl's Court) are listed on Airtasker; no specific band or school was confirmed.

blacksmithing.how: A two-hour introductory blacksmithing course runs at the forge on Stepney City Farm (ages 16+), with longer knife-forging days also offered.

leatherwork.how: Beginner leather workshops (hand-stitched wallet or accessory) run in London through CraftCourses and ClassBento, with materials and tools provided.

candle-making.how: Earl of East runs beginner candle-making workshops (about 90 minutes, soy candle to take home) at its Hackney base and King's Cross store.

japanese-language.how: The Japan Foundation London teaches Japanese at beginner and intermediate levels in term-time courses.

spanish-language.how: Instituto Cervantes London offers in-person and online Spanish courses for adults, teens and children at Devereux Court near Temple.

dungeons-and-dragons.how: RPG Taverns near London Bridge sells tickets for guided D&D sessions most days with dice and minis provided; board game cafes also host RPG nights.

trading-cards.how: Bad Moon Cafe (London Bridge and Waterloo) and Rogues Quarter (Kentish Town) host Magic: The Gathering and other card game events and trade.

trading-card-games.how: Bad Moon Cafe runs regular tournaments for Magic: The Gathering, Flesh and Blood and Warmachine; Rogues Quarter in Kentish Town hosts Magic events through the year.

wargaming-warhammer.how: Bad Moon Cafe has bespoke Warhammer tables, and BMC in Borough hosts weekly gaming nights with the London Wargaming Guild.

artisan-bread-baking.how: Bread Ahead Baking School teaches half-day to three-day bread, pastry and doughnut courses at Borough Market and Wembley.

chocolate-making.how: Bean-to-bar chocolate workshops (about 2 hours) run in Notting Hill via ClassBento; chocolatiers such as Hotel Chocolat and Melt also offer classes.

mixology.how: Two-hour mixologist-led cocktail-making classes and immersive cocktail experiences run across London, listed on Experience Days.

pasta-and-general-cooking-classes.how: Hands-on cooking classes run at cookery schools such as The Avenue Cookery and via ClassBento and Experience Days.

coffee-roasting.how: A four-hour home barista workshop is held at an historic London roastery with a roastery tour; hands-on roasting itself was not confirmed.
coffee-roasting.venue: Home barista workshop at a London roastery (ClassBento)

latte-art.how: Kaffeine runs evening latte art classes (about two hours, since 2010) at its Eastcastle Street cafe; Kiss the Hippo and ClassBento also run latte art workshops.

homebrewing-beer.how: London Beer Lab in Brixton runs small-group workshops where participants brew about 20 litres of all-grain beer and return to bottle it.

beekeeping-honey.how: The Hiver Experience in Kennington offers a hive inspection and honey beer tasting, and Hen Corner in west London runs an introduction to beekeeping course.

pub-trivia.how: Pub quiz nights run weekly across London pubs, for example The Pub Quiz at The Old Queens Head and quiz nights at Brixton Jamm.

poetry-slam.how: Hammer & Tongue runs year-round slam nights with an open slam at each, mostly at The Book Club in Shoreditch; Bang Said The Gun and Out Spoken also run spoken word nights.
poetry-slam.venue: Hammer & Tongue at The Book Club

coding-meetups.how: London community coding meetups such as a beginner-to-expert Code & Chat group are listed in social groups; no specific organiser page was opened.

history-walks.how: London Guided Walks runs more than thirty themed history walks (Roman London, Pepys, Hampstead) for a flat per-person fee.

heritage-trails.how: The Mayor of London publishes free self-guided heritage walks and trails under London Unseen, and Historic England has self-guided tours of London.

windsurfing.how: Welsh Harp Sailing Club on the Brent Reservoir offers windsurfing with free novice training for members on Thursday evenings; Docklands Sailing and Watersports Centre also runs beginner windsurfing courses.

sauna.how: Skuna Boats runs a wood-fired sauna boat at West India Quay in Canary Wharf with shared drop-in sessions and a cold plunge.

charcoal-life-drawing.how: City Lit runs life drawing and portraiture courses, and London Life Drawing and London Bridge Life Drawing hold drop-in sessions in community venues.

creative-writing.how: Southbank Centre hosts monthly three-hour Out-Spoken poetry masterclasses led by leading poets; City Lit and Faber Academy also teach writing.

perfumery.how: Half-day and two-hour perfume-making classes run in London, including Experimental Perfume Club in Covent Garden and The London Refinery in Notting Hill.

archery.how: London Archers run beginner courses in winter and have-a-go sessions in summer, shooting indoors in Pimlico and outdoors near Kensington Palace; other clubs include 2020 Archery at London Bridge.

bmx.how: Kimber Skatepark in Wandsworth combines a skatepark and BMX track, and BMX riders also use Southbank.

bouldering.how: Dedicated bouldering gyms include HarroWall, VauxWall, The Arch (Bermondsey, Acton, Edgware) and The Climbing Hangar, with shoe rental.

cricket.how: Adult cricket clubs and leagues operate across London, including Regent's Park Cricket Club and Last Man Stands adult leagues.

curling.how: Queens Ice and Bowl in Queensway has curling lanes on its ice rink.

dinghy-sailing.how: Welsh Harp Sailing Club, Wembley Sailing Club and Sea Cadets sail dinghies on the Brent Reservoir in north-west London.

fencing.how: Central London Fencing Club teaches beginners at Greycoat Hospital School; most London clubs offer a taster session before a multi-week beginner course.

gaelic-football-hurling.how: London GAA runs Gaelic football and hurling clubs (e.g. Dulwich Harps, Brothers Pearse) with county grounds at McGovern Park in Ruislip.

horse-riding.how: Hyde Park Stables offers arena riding lessons and courses for all abilities with no prior experience needed.

ice-hockey.how: Lee Valley Ice Centre offers ice hockey and Alexandra Palace hosts regular ice hockey matches.

ice-skating.how: Year-round rinks include Alexandra Palace, Lee Valley Ice Centre, Streatham Ice Arena and Queens in Queensway, plus seasonal rinks at Somerset House.

rock-climbing-top-rope.how: Roped climbing with an induction is available at Westway Climbing Centre, The Castle Climbing Centre and Mile End Climbing Wall.

judo.how: The Budokwai in Knightsbridge is a long-established judo club with beginner programmes; Sobell and Ealing judo clubs also operate.

lacrosse.how: Central London Lacrosse runs junior and adult teams based at the Regent's Park and Primrose Hill hub.

netball.how: Go Mammoth, Netbusters and Power Play run beginner and social netball leagues at many London venues.

padel.how: Dozens of padel clubs operate across London including Padium (Canary Wharf), Stratford Padel Club and pay-and-play public courts in Regent's Park and Hyde Park.

pickleball.how: The Padel Yard in Wandsworth lists an outdoor pickleball court; pickleball provision in London is still limited.

rugby.how: Adult rugby union clubs such as Belsize Park RFC play in Regent's Park; many more clubs exist across the metro area.

skateboarding.how: Southbank Undercroft is a famous skate spot, with further skateparks at Kimber (Wandsworth), Bay 66 and Cantelowes.

taekwondo.how: Taekwondo classes for beginners run at Elite Taekwon-Do (Kensington, Wembley), the Traditional Taekwondo Association (Peckham, Southwark) and London Taekwondo Warriors.

ultimate-frisbee.how: UK Ultimate lists clubs and runs tournaments at London venues such as Redbridge and Cranford; its find-a-club page covers London teams.

allotment-gardening.how: London has many council and private allotments, with demand at a record high according to a London Assembly report, including long-running sites such as Manor Garden Allotments in Hackney Wick.

urban-foraging.how: Wild Food UK runs foraging courses in the Surrey fringe of London including an autumn course at Warlingham.
urban-foraging.venue: Wild Food UK Warlingham foraging course

geocaching.how: Geocaching.com lists caches across London; its map defaults to central London.

hiking.how: The Capital Ring is a roughly 125 km waymarked circular walking route through London parks and green spaces, joinable at any point.

intertidal-walking.how: The tidal Thames foreshore can be explored at low tide, but searching it requires a Port of London Authority permit.

mountain-biking.how: Epping Forest permits mountain biking on its single-track trails, with clubs riding on Sunday mornings.

orienteering.how: Orienteering is a popular activity in Epping Forest on the north-east edge of London.

birds-of-prey-watching.how: The London Wetland Centre in Barnes is a major birdwatching site where sparrowhawks are among the species seen; large raptors are rare in the city.

stargazing.how: Hampstead Observatory is open to the public on winter Friday and Saturday evenings and Sunday mornings with volunteers from the Hampstead Scientific Society; the Royal Observatory Greenwich also has telescopes and a planetarium.

mushroom-foraging.how: Wild Food UK runs autumn foraging courses near London at Warlingham and in Surrey and Kent woodland.
mushroom-foraging.venue: Wild Food UK Warlingham foraging course

fishing.how: Fishing is permitted in some of the Highgate Ponds on Hampstead Heath; Lee Valley and Thames venues also exist.

hang-gliding.how: Greater London is flat with no suitable ridge launch sites; the nearest hang gliding is on the South Downs or Chilterns escarpments, roughly 1 to 1.5 hours away.

kayaking.how: Lee Valley White Water Centre at Waltham Cross offers canoeing and kayaking on Olympic and intermediate courses for all abilities.

kite-flying.how: Parliament Hill on Hampstead Heath is known as Kite Hill because it suits kite flying.

pedal-boating.how: Rowing boats and pedalos, including electric and accessible pedalos, can be hired on the Serpentine in Hyde Park.

rowing.how: Thames Rowing Club has rowed from Putney Embankment since 1860; many other tidal Thames clubs exist.

sailing.how: Welsh Harp Sailing Club and Wembley Sailing Club run sailing on the Brent Reservoir, and Phoenix Canoe Club offers sailing and canoeing there.

surfing-ocean.how: Greater London is inland with no ocean waves; the nearest regular surf is on the south coast around Bournemouth, roughly 2 to 2.5 hours away.

acting.how: RADA offers adult short courses in acting, improvisation and Meisner technique, some with no audition required.

ballet.how: The Royal Academy of Dance in London lists termly adult ballet classes; many other studios offer adult beginner ballet.

bharatanatyam.how: The Bhavan Centre stages Bharatanatyam performances and teaches Indian classical dance; a regular class timetable is on its site.

breakdancing.how: Pineapple Dance Studios in Covent Garden offers around 400 weekly open classes in over 40 styles, which include street dance.

choir.how: Morley College London offers Vocal Studies and Choirs courses open to adults.

dj-turntablism.how: Point Blank Music School in London teaches DJing and music production courses.

improv-comedy.how: Hoopla Impro runs beginner-friendly improv classes (Levels 1-5) and drop-in workshops in central London; The Comedy Store Players perform weekly.

kathak.how: Bhavan Centre in West Kensington hosts Kathak workshops and productions alongside Indian dance and music classes.

lion-dance.how: Lion dances are performed in Chinatown around Chinese New Year; no regular classes were confirmed.

magic.how: The Magic Circle's headquarters hosts regular close-up magic shows and tours, but its classes are for ages 10-18 only.

music-production.how: Point Blank Music School in London teaches music production and electronic music courses.

animation-2d.how: University of the Arts London short courses include an Animation, interactive, film and sound category taught in London.

bookbinding.how: London Centre for Book Arts in Hackney runs workshops and a making-books school with a bindery available to studio members.

film-photography-darkroom.how: Four Corners in Bethnal Green runs community darkroom facilities for film printing.

embroidery.how: Loop Knitting in Islington runs Embroidery and Textile classes and hand-stitching workshops.

jewellery-silversmithing.how: University of the Arts London short courses include an accessories and jewellery category in London.

knitting-crochet.how: Loop Knitting in Camden Passage runs knitting and crochet classes.

oil-painting.how: Morley College London offers Painting and Drawing courses for adults.

photography.how: University of the Arts London short courses include a Photography category covering digital photography in London.

pottery-handbuilding.how: Turning Earth runs six- to twelve-week all-level hand-building and wheel courses at studios in Hoxton, Leyton and Highgate.

pottery-wheel.how: Wheel-throwing taster and short courses run at London studios (Bankside, Nine Elms) and City Lit.

rug-tufting.how: Rug tufting workshops run in Nine Elms, Covent Garden and Wembley, listed on ClassBento.
rug-tufting.venue: Mini Rug Tufting Workshop (Nine Elms, ClassBento)

printmaking-screenprint.how: Screen printing courses run in Hackney, listed on ClassBento.

clay-sculpture.how: City Lit offers ceramics and sculpture courses in central London.

stained-glass.how: One-day and five-day lead stained glass courses run in London, and Morley College teaches an introductory stained glass course.
stained-glass.venue: Morley College Waterloo Centre stained glass course

weaving.how: Frame loom weaving workshops for beginners run in Catford and Wapping, listed on ClassBento.
weaving.venue: Learn to Weave on a Frame Loom workshop (Catford, ClassBento)

woodworking.how: Multi-day woodworking courses such as a two-day stool-making course run in Harlesden, listed on ClassBento.

watercolour-painting.how: Beginner watercolour workshops and a three-week course run in Shoreditch, listed on ClassBento.

3d-printing.how: London Hackspace and Machines Room offer 3D printers to members; South London Makerspace also has 3D printing.

laser-cutting.how: London Hackspace and Machines Room (FabLab) have laser cutters available to members.

cnc-machining.how: London Hackspace lists CNC equipment and Machines Room has CNC routers for members.

hackerspace-electronics.how: London Hackspace is a community-run workshop with electronics benches, and South London Makerspace in Herne Hill offers electronics too.

amateur-radio.how: Crystal Palace Radio and Electronics Club offers training for the amateur radio licence and meets in south London.
amateur-radio.venue: Crystal Palace Radio and Electronics Club

ctf-security.how: OWASP London has run capture-the-flag and hackathon evenings in central London; recent events were not confirmed.

hackathons.how: OWASP London ran a hackathon and CTF in the City; current hackathon calendars were not confirmed.

airsoft.how: Indoor airsoft runs at Ultimate Airsoft in Whitechapel and Bunker 51 in Charlton; outdoor sites exist in Surrey.

paintball.how: Paintball parks near the M25 such as AA Paintzone (Whyteleafe) and Campaign Paintball (Cobham) take walk-in groups.

arcade-games.how: Arcade bars such as Four Quarters and London Games Room (Shoreditch, London Bridge) offer retro arcade cabinets.

ten-pin-bowling.how: Bowling lanes are available at Lane7 Victoria and Gravity Wandsworth.

vr-gaming.how: VR arenas and booths include Sandbox VR in Holborn and DNA VR in Camden, Battersea and Hammersmith.

escape-rooms.how: Escape Hunt runs escape rooms at its Oxford Street venue, and other operators exist across London.

esports-gaming.how: Esports venues such as Meltdown (Caledonian Road) and Platform (Shoreditch) host competitive gaming.

parkour.how: Parkour Generations runs parkour classes across London including a beginner course.

birdwatching.how: London Wetland Centre in Barnes has wildlife sightings and runs birding events such as an Urban Birder course.

science-museum.how: The Science Museum in South Kensington has free admission (pre-booked ticket) and galleries such as Wonderlab, Space and Flight.

museums.how: Free national museums such as the Science Museum in South Kensington are open to visitors daily.

art-gallery.how: Tate Modern offers free entry to its collection displays on Bankside.

stamp-collecting.how: The Royal Philatelic Society London, based at 15 Abchurch Lane, welcomes stamp collectors and postal historians as members.

coin-collecting.how: The British Numismatic Society holds regular talks and gatherings; its London meeting place was not confirmed on its page.

ancient-ruins-excavation.how: The Thames Discovery Programme, run by MOLA, involves volunteers in recording archaeology on the Thames foreshore; this is survey and monitoring rather than a full dig.

animal-shelter-volunteering.how: Battersea offers kennel and cattery support roles and fostering volunteers at its London centre.

community-gardening.how: Spitalfields City Farm runs a volunteer programme with a dedicated growing section.

meetups.how: Meetup lists a large Games and Hobbies directory of groups in London.

chess.how: Meetup's London listing includes chess clubs and groups.

board-games.how: Meetup's London listing includes board game groups.

contract-bridge.how: Meetup's London listing includes bridge clubs and groups.

hot-spring-bathing.how: No natural hot springs exist in the London basin; the nearest, Thermae Bath Spa in Bath, is roughly 2 hours away by train.

safari.how: No free-roaming African safari exists near London; the nearest drive-through safari is Woburn Safari Park in Bedfordshire, about 1 hour by car.

big-wall-climbing.how: No big walls in the metro area; the Shawangunks (Gunks) cliffs, about 2 hours north, offer multi-pitch trad climbing, and true big walls need Yosemite or similar.

bobsled.how: No bobsled track in the metro area; the Olympic track at Lake Placid is about 5 hours north and sells tourist rides.

buzkashi.how: Central Asian horseback game needing a steppe horse culture; not played in the metro area.

camel-racing.how: Needs a camel-racing culture and tracks (Gulf states, Australia); none in the metro area.

cheese-rolling.how: Tied to a single hill in Gloucestershire, England; no equivalent event in the metro area.

elephant-polo.how: Needs working elephants (Nepal, Thailand, India); none in the metro area.

ski-jumping.how: No jumping hill in the metro area; the Olympic jumping complex at Lake Placid is about 5 hours north.

capoeira.how: ABADA-Capoeira runs adult and kids classes in a Midtown studio; Capoeira Angola classes also run in Manhattan.

drone-racing.how: The Drone Racing League is headquartered in NYC but is a pro circuit; a pay-per-race indoor venue (DroneRush) was listed, with current status unconfirmed.

ultimate-frisbee.how: DiscNY lists pickup games in Prospect, McCarren, Central and Riverside parks; Manhattan Ultimate Disc runs leagues with a recreational tier for beginners.

dragon-boat.how: Club crews train for the annual Hong Kong Dragon Boat Festival, raced on Meadow Lake in Flushing Meadows Corona Park with festival-supplied boats and paddles.
dragon-boat.venue: Hong Kong Dragon Boat Festival, Meadow Lake

urban-foraging.how: Naturalist Steve Brill leads paid foraging walks in Prospect Park and Central Park covering edible and medicinal wild plants.

mushroom-foraging.how: A 3-hour guided Prospect Park foraging walk covers edible and medicinal plants and mushrooms; a dedicated fungi walk listing exists but may be unavailable.

outrigger-canoe.how: New York Outrigger runs free novice sessions for outrigger canoeing from the Pier 96 boathouse on the Hudson (age 14+).

stand-up-paddleboarding.how: New York Outrigger offers free novice stand-up paddleboarding sessions from Pier 96, and Perfect Paddles runs paid SUP lessons in Brooklyn Bridge Park.

aerial-silks-circus.how: Circus Warehouse in Long Island City teaches flying and static trapeze and aerial classes; Trapeze School New York and Circus Academy New York also offer silks.

improv-comedy.how: The Peoples Improv Theater runs improv classes including weekend drop-in sessions.

ballet.how: Peridance Capezio Center teaches ballet and other dance at all levels in open classes.

irish-dance.how: The Irish Arts Center offers Irish dance classes alongside fiddle, harp and bodhran instruction.

orchestra.how: The Chelsea Symphony is a Manhattan community orchestra with a play-with-us page for musicians.

guitar.how: Greenwich House Music School gives guitar lessons for all levels, from first-timers up.

piano.how: Greenwich House Music School gives piano lessons for all levels, from first-timers up.

pole-dance.how: Body & Pole teaches pole classes from first-timers to professionals, with first-class offers for new students.

salsa-bachata.how: Drop-in salsa and bachata classes with socials run at Latin dance studios across Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx.

sitar.how: Chhandayan Center for Indian Music in Midtown Manhattan lists group sitar and tabla classes.

stand-up-comedy.how: Beginner stand-up courses of about six weeks end in a graduation show at a Manhattan comedy club.

swing-lindy-hop.how: Lindy hop series for beginners run at the 92nd Street Y and Chelsea studios, with no partner needed.

tabla.how: Chhandayan runs small-group tabla classes (10 students or fewer) for all ages and levels with an annual recital.

taiko.how: Soh Daiko, founded 1979 at the New York Buddhist Church, runs public taiko workshops and recruits members; Taikoza offers paid classes.

tap-dance.how: Beginner and adult tap classes are widely offered at Manhattan dance studios.

chinese-opera.how: Chinese (Peking) opera is performed by local societies such as the New York Chinese Opera Society and Yeh Yu; regular public classes are not clearly listed.

batik-painting.how: Textile Arts Center in Brooklyn lists a batik one-day intensive on its workshop calendar.

embroidery.how: Textile Arts Center in Brooklyn lists embroidery and bead embroidery workshops.

etching.how: Manhattan Graphics Center has practitioners in intaglio (including etching), relief, lithography and screenprint and runs classes.

lithography.how: Manhattan Graphics Center teaches lithography alongside intaglio, relief and screenprinting.

printmaking-screenprint.how: Manhattan Graphics Center offers screenprinting among its printmaking classes.

film-photography-darkroom.how: International Center of Photography runs courses through Open Education and has darkrooms and media labs; film and alternative processes are taught.

filmmaking.how: New York Film Academy offers filmmaking programmes and short-term workshops of 1 to 15 weeks.

glassblowing.how: UrbanGlass in Brooklyn runs Intro to Glassblowing and Glassblowing 101 classes for beginners.

lampworking.how: UrbanGlass lists Flameworking and Beadmaking classes such as Hot Torch Basics Bootcamp for beginners.

laser-cutting.how: NYC Resistor's shared space in downtown Brooklyn lists a laser cutter for members.

robotics-arduino.how: NYC Resistor hosts electronics classes (e.g. KiCad circuit board design) and members' maker projects.

origami.how: OrigamiUSA runs monthly Folding Sundays meetings and special sessions at the American Museum of Natural History.

3d-printing.how: Fat Cat Fab Lab, a volunteer-run makerspace in the West Village, offers 3D printing and a 3D Printing 101 class.

cnc-machining.how: Fat Cat Fab Lab has CNC routing with a members-only CNC safety class.

oil-painting.how: The Art Students League of New York offers painting classes at all levels on West 57th Street.
oil-painting.venue: Art Students League of New York

charcoal-life-drawing.how: The Art Students League of New York runs drawing classes, and life drawing is its long-standing core offering.
charcoal-life-drawing.venue: Art Students League of New York

clay-sculpture.how: The Art Students League of New York offers sculpture classes.
clay-sculpture.venue: Art Students League of New York

watercolour-painting.how: Brooklyn Brainery runs watercolor classes such as Watercolor Fundamentals and Watercolor Landscapes.

chocolate-making.how: Raaka Chocolate makes bean-to-bar chocolate in Red Hook and runs a 3.5 to 4 hour bean-to-bar class on weekends.

beekeeping-honey.how: NYC Beekeeping, a volunteer group, runs a Saturday Series hands-on course, mentoring, newcomer events and community honey harvests.

cosplay.how: New York Comic Con at the Javits Center holds cosplay competitions such as the Crown Championships of Cosplay.

vr-gaming.how: Sandbox VR lists a New York City location for group VR gaming.

pub-trivia.how: Sporcle Live runs pub trivia events with a Find a Game location finder; NYC bars host weekly quiz nights.

dim-sum-making.how: Hands-on dim sum and dumpling classes run at Chelsea Market (Buddakan) and ICE, with CocuSocial offering cheaper dumpling sessions.
dim-sum-making.venue: Buddakan dim sum class, Chelsea Market

sushi-making.how: Beginner sushi-rolling classes run by Taste Buds Kitchen, CocuSocial and others; ingredients and tools are supplied.

sake-tasting.how: Brooklyn Kura's Sake Studies Center runs guided sake tasting classes with a brewery tour, plus a taproom.

sake-making.how: Brooklyn Kura brews sake in Industry City and its classes include a brewery tour; hands-on brewing is limited to the tour and courses.

tea-ceremony.how: Beginner chanoyu (Japanese tea ceremony) classes are taught at Resobox in the East Village.

latte-art.how: Partners Coffee and other roasters teach barista and free-pour latte art classes for beginners.

sourdough-baking.how: NY Cake Academy teaches a two-hour sourdough class covering starter, kneading and baking.

whisky-society.how: The Scotch Malt Whisky Society hosts recurring guided tastings in Midtown Manhattan, and Drammers Whisky Club began as a NYC group.
whisky-society.venue: Scotch Malt Whisky Society NYC tastings

hawker-crawling.how: Guided and self-guided street-food crawls cover the food courts and stalls of Flushing's Chinatown, reached by the 7 train.

butterfly-watching.how: The AMNH Butterfly Conservatory houses hundreds of live butterflies, and Central Park's North Meadow butterfly gardens attract wild species in summer.

comic-collecting.how: Midtown Comics, Forbidden Planet and JHU Comic Books sell new and back-issue comics across Manhattan.

trading-cards.how: Chameleon Comics & Cards in the Financial District sells trading cards, and many comic and game shops host card-game play.

rock-fossil-collecting.how: NYC Parks rangers lead fossil walks at Wolfe's Pond Park on Staten Island, and hobbyists report fossil finds on Staten Island beaches.
rock-fossil-collecting.venue: Wolfe's Pond Park fossil exploration (NYC Parks)

sneaker-collecting.how: Flight Club on Broadway buys, consigns and sells rare and vintage sneakers.

train-spotting.how: The New York Transit Museum shows vintage subway cars in a retired station, runs Nostalgia Rides on vintage trains and a Grand Central gallery.

whale-watching.how: Gotham Whale runs whale and dolphin watching trips from Riis Landing in Rockaway, mostly humpbacks, May to November.

archival-research.how: The NYC Municipal Archives has public research rooms open by appointment.

genealogy.how: The Municipal Archives' 'Research Your Family History' programme points to its vital records collection, with research-room access.

creative-writing.how: Gotham Writers Workshop (now writingclasses.com) runs creative-writing classes in New York; the site refused automated access.

poetry-slam.how: The Nuyorican Poets Cafe runs the Bowery Slam, Final Friday Slam and weekly open mics at off-site venues during renovation.

history-walks.how: Big Onion Walking Tours has run guided two-hour history walks of about 20 neighbourhoods since 1991.

cultural-heritage-centres.how: The Museum of Chinese in America in Chinatown shows exhibitions and runs calligraphy workshops, screenings and performances.

wartime-history.how: The Intrepid Sea, Air & Space Museum is a WWII-era aircraft carrier museum on the Hudson.

public-lectures.how: 92NY on the Upper East Side hosts public lectures and talks; the site returned no text to the fetcher.

philosophy-cafe.how: The NYC Philosophy and Psychology Readers Community meetup runs reading and discussion sessions such as Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit.
philosophy-cafe.venue: NYC Philosophy and Psychology Readers Community

meetups.how: Meetup lists hundreds of NYC hobby groups, such as sketching, piano, songwriting and board games.

book-club.how: The Meetup NYC Philosophy and Psychology Readers Community reads set texts weekly, and many other reading groups are listed.
book-club.venue: NYC Philosophy and Psychology Readers Community

running-club.how: New York Road Runners organises races and group runs in Central Park; the page sat behind a queue at fetch time.

volunteering.how: New York Cares lists over 1,000 volunteer opportunities in tutoring, food, gardening and more.

support-groups.how: NAMI-NYC Metro runs peer support groups led by trained volunteers with lived experience.

meditation.how: New York Insight Meditation Center runs sittings and classes in Manhattan.

pet-adoption.how: Animal Care Centers of NYC run adoption centres in all five boroughs.

indoor-snow-play.how: Big SNOW at American Dream offers real-snow tubing and snow play year-round, just over the river in New Jersey.

snow-skiing.how: Big SNOW at American Dream offers year-round indoor skiing and snowboarding with lessons, and real mountains need a 2-3 hour drive.

rodeo.how: PBR bull riding comes to Madison Square Garden each January as a one-off event, with no regular local rodeo.
rodeo.venue: Madison Square Garden (PBR Buck Off at the Garden)

outdoor-skydiving.how: No drop zone operates in the dense metro area; Skydive Long Island at Shirley is about 55 miles east, roughly 1.5 hours by car.

bullfighting.how: Bullfighting is not practised in the US; the nearest legal bullrings are in Mexico or Spain, a flight away.

canyoning.how: No suitable gorges exist in the metro area; the nearest canyoning is in the Adirondacks or Appalachians, several hours away.

cave-diving.how: The area has no flooded caves; the nearest cave diving is in Florida, a flight away.

dog-sledding.how: No snow-reliable terrain exists locally; the nearest dog sledding is in the Adirondacks, several hours away.

glacier-trekking.how: No glaciers exist nearby; the nearest are in Alaska, Canada or Iceland.

luge.how: There is no luge track nearby; the nearest is the Olympic track at Lake Placid, about 5 hours north.

volcano-boarding.how: No volcanoes exist in the region; the activity is offered at Cerro Negro in Nicaragua.

sandboarding-desert.how: No desert exists locally; real sandboarding and desert trekking means the US Southwest or beyond, a flight away.

white-water-rafting.how: No whitewater exists in the metro area; the nearest rafting is on the Delaware or Lehigh rivers, roughly 2 hours away.

mountaineering.how: No alpine terrain exists locally; the nearest mountaineering is in the Adirondacks, about 4-5 hours north.

cave-exploring.how: No natural caves exist in the metro area; the nearest show caves such as Howe Caverns are about 2.5 hours north.

ancient-ruins-excavation.how: No ancient ruins exist in the region; excavation field schools are abroad in the Mediterranean or Latin America.

base-jumping.how: BASE jumping from city structures is illegal; the legal organised event is Bridge Day in West Virginia, about 7 hours away.

hiking.how: NYC Parks lists marked hiking trails (Staten Island Greenbelt, Van Cortlandt, Pelham Bay) and runs guided hikes with Urban Park Rangers.

rowing.how: Row New York offers free beginner rowing lessons at Paerdegat Basin, and Sebago Canoe Club hosts community open houses with rowing outings on Jamaica Bay.
rowing.venue: Row New York / Paerdegat Basin Community Dock

jewellery-silversmithing.how: Ring-making and silversmithing classes run at Ayaka Nishi Jewelry Design School and other studios listed on CourseHorse; tools and materials are supplied.

birdwatching.how: Central Park's Ramble and Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge are major birding sites, with NYC Bird Alliance guiding birders to sites across the five boroughs.
birdwatching.venue: Central Park Ramble / Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge

dinghy-sailing.how: Riverdale Yacht Club (Bronx) has taught sailing on Optimist, Laser and 420 dinghies; Hudson River Community Sailing and Atlantic Yachting teach small-boat and keelboat sailing on the Hudson.

sailing.how: Offshore Sailing School runs lessons from North Cove Marina in Battery Park, and Hudson River Community Sailing offers beginner classes from its boathouse.

geocaching.how: Geocaching.com lists active caches in NYC parks such as Cunningham Park.

mountain-biking.how: Cunningham Park in Queens has about 6.5 miles of graded mountain-bike trails built and maintained by the CLIMB volunteer group.

scuba-diving.how: PADI Open Water courses with a Manhattan pool run at Scuba Network and Scuba.com New York, and Captain Mike's Diving Services on City Island is a 5-star PADI facility.

bharatanatyam.how: Aalokam NY teaches Bharatanatyam to adults and children in Manhattan and Brooklyn with a free trial class; Dakshina Palli also teaches in Midtown.

dj-turntablism.how: Scratch DJ Academy (Cooper Square), Dubspot and Garnish Music Production School teach DJing and turntablism in small classes.

music-production.how: Garnish Music Production School and Dubspot run Ableton Live, Logic Pro and mixing courses with 4-student classes.

bookbinding.how: Brooklyn Craft Company runs a beginner Bookbinding 101 class (long-stitch journal) and Manifesto in Gowanus offers bookbinding workshops.

leatherwork.how: Leatherworking workshops to make wallets and cases run at Brooklyn studios listed on CourseHorse, including Manifesto in Gowanus.

tango.how: NY Tango School holds weekly beginner group classes and a milonga practice; no partner or experience required.

chinese-orchestra.how: The Chinese Music Ensemble of New York (founded 1961) is a Chinese orchestra with concerts and lessons; Columbia Chinese Orchestra is a student group.
chinese-orchestra.venue: Chinese Music Ensemble of New York

erhu.how: The Chinese Music Ensemble of New York lists private lessons including erhu.
erhu.venue: Chinese Music Ensemble of New York

guzheng.how: China Institute in Lower Manhattan launched guqin, erhu and guzheng classes; private teachers also advertise in NYC.

gamelan.how: Gamelan Kusuma Laras (Javanese) and Gamelan Dharma Swara (Balinese) are community ensembles based at the Indonesian Consulate in Manhattan.

lion-dance.how: Troupes such as New York United Lion and Dragon Dance Troupe practise in Sara D. Roosevelt Park, and W.O.W. Project and NY Choy Lay Fut run lion dance teams in Chinatown.

fishing.how: Catch-and-release fishing is allowed at Central Park's Harlem Meer (NY State licence needed for ages 16+), with Central Park Conservancy fishing programs and bamboo-pole loans when running.

freshwater-fishing.how: Harlem Meer in Central Park holds largemouth bass, sunfish, carp and chain pickerel and is open to catch-and-release angling.

board-games.how: Board game cafes such as Hex & Co. (500+ games, walk-in cover charge), The Uncommons and The Brooklyn Strategist let visitors play from large libraries.

esports-gaming.how: Waypoint on the Lower East Side is a gaming cafe with 30 PCs for titles such as League of Legends and Fortnite.

curling.how: CurlNYC and Brooklyn Lakeside Curling Club run learn-to-curl sessions and leagues on Prospect Park's ice; Long Island Curling Club curls at Syosset.

vinyl-records.how: Dozens of independent record stores including Academy Records, Rough Trade NYC, Generation Records and Brooklyn Record Exchange sell new and used vinyl.

pasta-and-general-cooking-classes.how: CocuSocial, Red Inside Culinary and Murray's Cheese run hands-on fresh pasta classes in Manhattan.

artisan-bread-baking.how: NY Cake Academy offers a Bread Making Certificate Series and focaccia classes.

dog-parks.how: NYC has fenced dog runs (Tompkins Square, Chelsea Waterside, Carl Schurz Park) and park areas that allow off-leash dogs before 9am and after 9pm.

flamenco.how: Ballet Hispanico School of Dance offers adult flamenco classes open to all levels, and Flamenco Vivo Carlota Santana runs classes at its Center for Flamenco Arts.

safari.how: No free-roaming wildlife safari exists in the metro area; the nearest drive-through safari is Six Flags Great Adventure in Jackson, New Jersey, about 1.5 hours away, and the Bronx Zoo only has enclosed exhibits.

hot-spring-bathing.how: There are no natural geothermal springs in the New York metro area; the nearest are in Berkeley Springs, West Virginia, roughly 5 hours away (Korean spas such as Spa Castle in Queens use heated pools instead).

hunting.how: Firearm discharge and hunting are banned in the five boroughs; the nearest deer hunting is on Long Island's east end and in the Hudson Valley, roughly 1.5-2 hours away.

hang-gliding.how: The metro area has no launch ridges; the nearest hang gliding is at Ellenville in the Shawangunks, about 2 hours away, or Kitty Hawk Kites' tow operation in New Jersey.

sup-yoga.how: Manhattan Kayak Company runs SUP yoga classes and A-Team Paddleboarding in Rockaway Park offers yoga on paddleboards.

disc-golf.how: Highland Park Disc Golf Course, a 10-hole permanent course opened in 2024 on the Brooklyn/Queens border, was built by the NYC Disc Golf Association with NYC Parks.

choir.how: Everybody Sing New York is a free no-audition weekly community choir on the Upper West Side, and Washington Heights Community Choir is a no-audition adult chorus.

museums.how: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, MoMA, the Guggenheim and many others are open daily to visitors.

art-gallery.how: MoMA and the Guggenheim show modern and contemporary art, and Chelsea has a dense cluster of free commercial galleries.

hackathons.how: Tech Week's NYC calendar lists hackathons across Manhattan and Brooklyn each June, alongside university-hosted events at NYU and Columbia.

amateur-radio.how: The ARRL club directory lists Queens clubs offering entry-level licence classes and test sessions, including Hall of Science Amateur Radio Club and ARC Emergency Communications Service.
amateur-radio.venue: Hall of Science Amateur Radio Club

ctf-security.how: Anarcho-Tech NYC runs a beginner-friendly CTF team and NYU's Cybersecurity Club holds weekly HackNights and CTF101 sessions.

coding-meetups.how: OWASP New York City holds open application-security meetups, and many developer meetups and NYU/Columbia tech clubs run regular events.

acting.how: HB Studio in Greenwich Village teaches acting classes, one of many conservatories and studios offering adult courses.

nature-guided-walks.how: NYC Parks Urban Park Rangers and partner groups lead free guided hikes and nature walks through the city's parks.

escape-rooms.how: The Escape Game NYC in Midtown and many other operators run one-hour themed escape rooms.

archery.how: Indoor archery ranges with intro classes, lane rentals and leagues operate in Gowanus and the Lower East Side; NYC Parks rangers also run free archery on Staten Island.

bmx.how: The city's Harold Ickes Playground skate and BMX park in Red Hook opened in 2024; BMX-specific programming is limited.

bouldering.how: VITAL and Brooklyn Boulders run indoor bouldering gyms with day passes and shoe rental.

cricket.how: Cricket is widely played on park pitches such as Van Cortlandt Park by the NYC Cricket League and community clubs; cricket became a varsity sport in city schools in 2008.

fencing.how: Tim Morehouse Fencing Club, Manhattan Fencing Center and New Amsterdam Fencing Academy run adult beginner classes with loaner gear.

gaelic-football-hurling.how: New York GAA, founded 1914, fields hurling and Gaelic football teams that play at Gaelic Park in the Bronx.

horse-riding.how: Riding lessons and trail rides are available at Brooklyn and Bronx stables such as Kensington Stables beside Prospect Park.

ice-hockey.how: Chelsea Piers Sky Rink runs year-round adult leagues and learn-to-play classes, and Central Park's Davis Center has an adult league.

ice-skating.how: Public skating is offered at Central Park's Wollman Rink, Bryant Park, Rockefeller Center and Chelsea Piers, with skate rental.

rock-climbing-top-rope.how: Central Rock Gym on the Upper West Side and Brooklyn gyms offer top rope, auto-belay and lead climbing with rentals.
rock-climbing-top-rope.venue: Central Rock Gym Upper West Side

judo.how: Judo is taught in dojos such as Hoteikan Dojo in Bay Ridge and Staten Island Judo Jujitsu Dojo.

padel.how: Padel Haus runs indoor padel courts in Brooklyn and Replay offers padel and pickleball.

pickleball.how: CityPickle runs pay-to-play pickleball courts at Wollman Rink in Central Park, and indoor venues such as Replay exist.

rugby.how: Several amateur rugby union clubs play around the city, listed at nycrugby.com.

skateboarding.how: Free public skateparks include Pier 62, LES Skatepark under the Manhattan Bridge, Astoria Skate Plaza and Red Hook.

snowboarding.how: Big SNOW American Dream in East Rutherford, NJ, is an indoor real-snow slope with lesson programs; outdoor resorts are 1.5-2.5 hours away.

taekwondo.how: Taekwondo schools such as Ahns' Taekwondo NYC and West Side Taekwondo offer adult and kids classes.

allotment-gardening.how: GreenThumb supports hundreds of community gardens across the five boroughs where residents can join and garden plots.

camping.how: Camping is possible at Floyd Bennett Field in Brooklyn (permit based) and at nearby state and county campgrounds.

hydroponics-urban-farming.how: Brooklyn Grange operates soil-based rooftop farms in Queens and the Brooklyn Navy Yard with farm visits and events.

kayaking.how: Downtown Boathouse offers free walk-up kayaking on the Hudson at Pier 26 from May to October.

surfing-ocean.how: Ocean surfing with lessons and board rental is available at Rockaway Beach in Queens, reached by subway or ferry.

mangrove-sea-kayaking.how: Mangroves do not grow in the New York climate; the nearest guided mangrove kayaking is in Florida, about a 2.5 hour flight.

macrame.how: The New York Sewing Center teaches macrame alongside knitting and needlepoint classes.

perfumery.how: Bios Apothecary runs a natural perfume workshop where participants take home a 15ml bottle; Back Porch Soap Company also lists custom perfume classes.

photography.how: The School at ICP runs open-enrolment photography courses and workshops for all skill levels.
photography.venue: International Center of Photography (The School at ICP)

pottery-handbuilding.how: Greenwich House Pottery teaches handbuilding to all levels at its Jones Street and Chelsea studios.

pottery-wheel.how: Greenwich House Pottery offers wheel-throwing classes for first-timers upward; Pottery NYC also runs wheel courses.

rug-tufting.how: Craftsman Ave in Industry City runs tufting wall-art and rug classes using a tufting gun; other studios list punch-needle and tufting workshops.

stained-glass.how: UrbanGlass in Fort Greene offers stained glass suncatcher, projects and sampler classes.

weaving.how: CourseHorse lists multiple weaving classes in NYC, including Saori weaving, though the operating studio was not confirmed.

woodworking.how: Craftsman Ave teaches beginner woodworking, including a two-day side-table build, in a professional shop.

hackerspace-electronics.how: NYC Resistor in downtown Brooklyn is a long-running member hackerspace with workshops such as KiCad PCB design; Hack Manhattan holds open houses on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

chess.how: Marshall Chess Club in Greenwich Village offers adult classes, instruction and tournaments; casual chess also runs in Washington Square Park.

contract-bridge.how: Honors Bridge Club in Manhattan is a long-established duplicate bridge club (founded 1993).

arcade-games.how: Barcade operates classic-arcade bars in Chelsea, FiDi, St. Marks Place and Brooklyn.

dungeons-and-dragons.how: Twenty Sided Store hosts weekly beginner-friendly D&D sessions with materials provided.

trading-card-games.how: Twenty Sided Store runs Magic: The Gathering events and prereleases.

mahjong.how: New mahjong social clubs and pop-up game nights have multiplied across the city.

ten-pin-bowling.how: Brooklyn Bowl is a bowling alley and music venue with lane rentals and a restaurant.

homebrewing-beer.how: Brooklyn Brew Shop sells beer-making kits and mixes and hard-cider kits for apartment homebrewing.

fermentation-kombucha.how: Brooklyn Brew Shop sells kombucha kits, fermented hot sauce kits and fermentation supplies for home use.

science-museum.how: The New York Hall of Science in Queens is a hands-on science museum.

japanese-language.how: Japan Society's Language Center teaches Japanese across 13 levels in 10- and 5-week sessions.

spanish-language.how: Instituto Cervantes New York runs Spanish courses in person and online.

heritage-trails.how: Municipal Art Society runs guided historic and architectural walking tours of neighbourhoods such as SoHo, Grand Central and Bed-Stuy.

sauna.how: The Russian & Turkish Baths in the East Village have a redwood sauna, Russian and Turkish rooms.

cold-plunge.how: The Russian & Turkish Baths list an ice-cold pool alongside the sauna.

taiko.how: Matsuriza Taiko, a metro Atlanta Japanese drum troupe, performs at JapanFest and community events, but no regular open beginner classes were confirmed.

tea-ceremony.how: The Chado Urasenke Tankoukai Atlanta Association meets at Nakato Restaurant and tea ceremony workshops appear at the annual JapanFest.

pottery-wheel.how: Chastain Arts Center's pottery studio runs eight-to-nine-week wheel-throwing courses for beginners and intermediate students on weekday and weekend slots.

perfumery.how: INDIEHOUSE runs guided custom-perfume workshops using professional perfumer's oils, with each guest taking home a 30 ml bottle.

irish-dance.how: Atlanta Irish Dance by Burke Connolly teaches Irish dance to all ages and abilities at its Faulkner Road studio and branches in Marietta, Decatur and Sandy Springs.

mahjong.how: 1 Dot Mah Jongg, Two Sparrows and Atlanta Mahjong Studio run lessons, guided play and leagues, and a Decatur social club hosts supervised beginner games.

outdoor-rock-climbing.how: Boat Rock, a granite bouldering area southwest of the city, offers hundreds of boulder problems in the Greater Atlanta area, with classics such as Yellow Wall Arete.

geocaching.how: Stone Mountain Park hosts long-running caches including the multi-cache tour of Stone Mountain, and Atlanta has thousands of caches in city parks.

camping.how: Stone Mountain Park offers a campground plus yurt rental sites inside the park.

nature-guided-walks.how: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area offers ranger-led hikes, and Chattahoochee Nature Center runs trail and education programs.

orienteering.how: The Georgia Orienteering Club holds regular park events with a beginner guide, though many courses are in state parks beyond the metro radius.

birds-of-prey-watching.how: Chattahoochee Nature Center in Roswell has licensed wildlife staff rehabilitating birds of prey with resident raptors on display, plus riverside trails for wild hawks.

coastal-cleanup.how: No beach exists in the metro area, but Chattahoochee Riverkeeper's annual Sweep the Hooch river cleanup has dozens of sites in Metro Atlanta counties and the national recreation area.

genealogy.how: The National Archives at Atlanta in Morrow holds federal records for eight southeastern states, with a research room open by appointment.

meetups.how: Meetup lists large Atlanta groups for hiking, board games, mahjong, crafts and journaling, with weekly events.

latte-art.how: Opo Coffee Training Lab in Decatur runs small beginner latte-art classes led by an SCA-authorized trainer.

cultural-heritage-centres.how: The APEX Museum on Sweet Auburn Avenue preserves and presents Black history with exhibits on the Sweet Auburn district.

creative-writing.how: The Atlanta Writers Club holds monthly meetings and periodic workshops, with critique groups across the metro and a free first visit.

dim-sum-making.how: Cozymeal and Classbento list chef-led Chinese and dumpling-making classes in Atlanta covering folding techniques and dim sum menus.

sourdough-baking.how: Atlanta Botanical Garden runs Sourdough 101 classes where each student takes home a starter, and The Cook's Warehouse in Midtown offers hands-on sourdough classes.

chocolate-making.how: XOCOLATL Small Batch Chocolate at Krog Street Market offers micro-factory tours and bean-to-bar tastings, though hands-on making classes were not confirmed as ongoing.

fermentation-kombucha.how: Cultured South, a kombucha taproom on the BeltLine Westside Trail, hosts occasional fermentation classes and Atlanta Utility Works runs hands-on fermentation events.

tango.how: Local teachers run beginner to advanced Argentine tango classes through Meetup and a weekly class at Daza Dance on Peachtree Road.

drone-racing.how: Georgia Tech's RotorJackets host MultiGP regional qualifier races at Couch Park Field, and the DRC Atlanta chapter races FPV drones.

sup-yoga.how: Atlanta SUP Yoga holds seasonal sessions, including night classes, on Lake Lanier and earlier reports mention classes at Morgan Falls on the Chattahoochee.
